Subject: Reranker integration - post-call items

Hi Marissa / team,

Thanks again for the demo today — good call. Quick recap and a few follow-ups we discussed on the call:

- Goal: Improve our site search relevancy by adding a learned reranker on top of our existing lexical results.
- Primary asks:
  1) How Redwood's ranking API returns top_k results and score breakdowns
  2) Suggested top_k tuning and latency trade-offs
  3) What evaluation artifacts/data you need to run a first-pass relevance test (MRR / nDCG)
  4) SDK/auth guidance for our infra team

Attaching a first-pass evaluation spec (initial_eval_spec.xlsx) with sample queries and a short list of target URLs.

Next steps from our side: Priya will send a 2-3 day sample of anonymized query logs if that helps. From Redwood, would like a quick note on the minimal integration for a PoC and any recommended metric thresholds.

Questions for you now:
- Does the reranker API return full ranked lists (score + metadata) or just re-ranked ids?
- Can we request top_k per-call (e.g., top_k=10) and get scores suitable for offline evaluation?
- Any constraints on embedding dimensionality or required pre-processing?

Thanks — happy to hop on a short follow-up call if helpful.

Best,
Alex

Subject: Re: Reranker integration - post-call items

Alex — thanks for the clear recap and for sending the spec. Appreciate the context.

Short answers up front:
- Redwood's reranker returns full ranked lists by default: id, score, optional metadata. You can request top_k per call. Scores are provided as floating point logits/probabilities (configurable).
- Yes, the responses are suitable for offline evaluation; we also export a CSV-friendly evaluation output if you want us to run the first pass.
- Embedding constraints: we support common dimensions (256/512/768) and provide client-side SDK helpers for normalization; will confirm your model's expected dim.

Next steps I propose:
1) Engineering sync: Marcus + Dev can clarify API shape and minimal SDK setup (auth tokens, routing).
2) Send sample logs + target doc IDs (Priya) — we'll scope the eval and return MRR / nDCG / Recall@k along with latency profiles.
3) Decide PoC targets & timeline (we typically do a 2-week eval including a small A/B plan).

Marcus / Dev — can you add brief notes on SDK setup, auth flow (token/keys), and any routing considerations (dedicated vs hosted) for Searchly?

I'll also add a short checklist for data format and sample sizes.

Thanks,
Marissa
Marissa Cole

Thanks Marissa — adding the engineering details Alex asked for. Short tech note:

API & response shape (high level):
- POST /v1/rerank
  - body: { query: string, candidates: [id], top_k: int (optional), return_embeddings: bool (optional) }
  - response: { results: [{ id: string, score: float, metadata: { source: string, url: string } }], timings: { model_ms: int, total_ms: int } }

Scoring details: scores are normalized floats (0-1) by default; we can also return raw logits if you prefer. We include per-item metadata and can surface the embedding vector if you set return_embeddings=true (note: embedding serialization increases payload size).

Top_k & tuning guidance:
- Default recommended top_k for site reranking: 10.
- For offline eval: compute nDCG@5 and nDCG@10, MRR, and Recall@10. Tune top_k by trading off tail recall vs latency.
- Latency: typical model + infra for top_k=10 is ~35-70ms/model on dedicated capacity; hosted varies. We can provide a latency profile for your query length distribution.

Embeddings & pre-processing:
- We support 256/512/768 dims. If you have existing embeddings, we can accept them for hybrid scoring or re-encode with our encoder. Normalize vectors (L2) on client-side if you plan to use cosine similarity.

Evaluation plan & sample size:
- Minimum: 2k query-doc pairs with relevance labels (binary or graded). Ideal: 10k+ for stable nDCG estimates.
- If you only have implicit feedback (clicks), we can bootstrap with click-weighted labels but prefer human-labeled pairs for initial benchmarks.

Data format checklist (we can provide a template):
- CSV with columns: query_id, query_text, doc_id, relevance (0/1/2), doc_url, timestamp
- Candidate pool file (per query) with lexical baseline ranks + doc metadata

Attachments: reranker_api_spec.md, topk_tuning_guide.pdf (high-level guides)

Dev & infra notes:
- Auth: simple API token in Authorization header (Bearer). For Dedicated/private we support mTLS + KMS-based keys.
- SDKs: we have Python and Node SDKs; minimal integration is a POST to /v1/rerank from your backend after the lexical pass.
- Routing: for production you can set a routing policy by user segment (e.g., paid vs free) to send paid users to Dedicated capacity for tighter latency SLAs.

Happy to pair with your infra team for a short integration walkthrough.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Engineer, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference

This is great, thanks Marcus / Marissa. A few clarifying Qs before we send the sample: 

1) For offline eval, do you recommend labeling using graded relevance (0/1/2) or binary? We can do either; wondering about metric sensitivity.
2) If we supply our top-20 lexical candidates per query, is that sufficient for the PoC?
3) About embedding dims — our existing vectors are 512. If we send ours, will Redwood's scoring pipeline accept them directly for hybrid scoring, or do you recommend re-encoding?
4) Typical turnaround for the initial run (2k labeled pairs)?

We've attached a small seed (searchly_eval_seed.zip) with 500 queries and candidate pools to start. Can you confirm receipt and a rough ETA for the initial pass? Also curious about what threshold of delta (e.g., nDCG improvement) you'd consider material for an internal stakeholder review.

Happy to schedule a follow-up if needed.

—Alex
